figures.label: Figure 4-20a
figures.description: Two-well electric log correlation panel (labeled '(a)') comparing Well No. A-2 (DEVIATED WELL, left) with Well No. A-1 (VERTICAL WELL, right). Each well shows an SP curve on the left of the depth track and an AMPLIFIED SHORT NORMAL resistivity curve on the right; the resistivity curves are annotated 'RESISTIVITY PATTERN'. Correlation markers SRM NO. 1, SRM NO. 2, SRM NO. 3 and SRM NO. 4 are drawn as dashed tie lines between the wells, along with 'TOP OF 10,000' SD.' The deviated well A-2 shows the full section: 10,000' SAND, SRM NO. 2, SRM NO. 3, 10,300' SAND, SRM NO. 4. The vertical well A-1 lacks SRM NO. 2 and shows the 10,000' SAND directly overlying SRM NO. 3, with an arrow labeled 'MISSING SECTION 225'' at the fault cut. A stippled wedge/triangle spans between the two wells, tapering from the full interval on the A-2 side to a point at the fault in A-1; a vertical bracket in A-2 is annotated 'INTERVAL FAULTED OUT OF WELL No. A-1 225 FEET'. The figure demonstrates how detailed correlation of a deviated well against a vertical well locates the fault depth and determines the 225 ft missing section in the vertical well.

figures.label: Figure 4-22
figures.description: Three-dimensional block diagram of a dipping bed (upper and lower bed boundaries shown as inclined parallel planes) penetrated by a deviated wellbore. Origin T is at the top where the wellbore first penetrates the bed, at the upper right of the block. A spherical coordinate system is drawn with the X-axis horizontal in the direction of bed dip, the Y-axis horizontal and perpendicular to X, and the Z-axis vertical (Z and a second dashed segment labelled Z' are shown within the block). Angles labelled: \phi = dip of bed, marked twice (once at the left between the dipping bed boundary and horizontal, once in the interior between the dashed X-direction line and the vertical Z line, with a right-angle symbol adjacent); \psi = wellbore drift angle, at T between the vertical TVT line and the wellbore trace; \alpha = delta azimuth, in the horizontal base plane between the Y direction and the X direction. The heavy dashed line from T through the bed is labelled WELLBORE and MLT (measured log thickness); vertical lines labelled TVT (true vertical thickness) are shown at the right of T and in the interior. The left face of the block is labelled BED BOUNDARIES. The figure defines the geometry used to derive the general three-dimensional thickness correction factor.  Caption: A three-dimensional spherical coordinate system with one horizontal axis in the direction of bed dip (x-axis), one axis perpendicular to the first and also horizontal (y-axis), and finally, one axis perpendicular to the other two (z-axis). (Published by permission of D. Tearpock.)

equations.name: Missing section correction for wellbore deviation
variables: \psi = well bore deviation angle
LOG THICKNESS = 225 ft measured along deviated hole

figures.label: Figure 4-20b
figures.description: Simplified stratigraphic cross-section (part b) comparing a deviated well and a vertical well to show how an exaggerated (measured) fault cut in a deviated hole is corrected to true missing section. Left/center: an inclined wellbore (deviated Well No. A-2, hole deviation 48 degrees, marked at two places) is drawn across a stack of correlation markers — SRM NO. 1, SRM NO. 2, SRM NO. 3 and SRM NO. 4 (dash-dot correlation lines) plus the 10,000' SAND and the 10,300' SAND. Log curves (SP on the left of the hole trace and AMPLIFIED SHORT NORMAL / RESISTIVITY PATTERN on the right) are hung along the deviated hole, with depth ticks at 10,000' and 10,500'. A shaded/stippled band across the deviated hole between SRM No. 2 and SRM No. 3 level is annotated '225 FEET' — the exaggerated section measured along hole. Right: the vertical WELL NO. A-1 electric log (SP on the left, AMPLIFIED SHORT NORMAL on the right) with depth marks 10000' and 10500', showing SRM NO. 1, TOP OF 10,000' SAND, the 10,000' SAND, BASE F/O, SRM NO. 3, TOP OF 10,300' SAND, the 10,300' SAND, SRM NO. 4, and the LOWER PART OF RESISTIVITY (curve). The A-1 log is 'PULLED APART TO SHOW SECTION FAULTED OUT ±150 FEET'. An inset box gives the correction: MISSING SECTION = (LOG THICKNESS)(cos psi) = (225')(cos 48 deg) = (225')(0.669) = 150 FEET, with a right triangle labelled 225' hypotenuse, 48 degree angle, and 150' vertical leg; psi = well bore deviation angle. A scale bar at lower right shows 100' vertical and 100'–0 horizontal. Takeaway: the 225 ft of section measured along the 48-degree deviated hole corresponds to only 150 ft of true vertical missing (faulted-out) section, matching the fault cut seen in vertical Well A-1.

figures.label: Figure 4-21 (a)
figures.description: Schematic cross section of a dipping formation (two parallel bed boundaries, top and base, dipping to the right at angle φ) cut by a vertical reference line with a derrick symbol at surface. Two deviated well paths cross the beds: one labelled 'Type 1' with wellbore angle ψ1 (deviated well drilled up-dip, opposite to bed dip) and one labelled 'Type 2' with angle ψ2 (deviated well drilled down-dip, same direction as bed dip). figures.label: Figure 4-21 (b)
figures.description: TYPE 1 detailed wellbore/formation geometry used to derive the Type 1 correction factor. Shows Formation Top and Formation Base as parallel dipping lines, a directionally drilled well crossing them from lower-left (point M) to upper-right (point T), with perpendicular construction lines to points C and E (right-angle symbols) and a vertical line down to point V. Angles labelled: ζ between well path and formation, ψ1, ρ at M, β at M, and apparent dip φ_a at M, at the vertical leg, and at V. Accompanying relations: ψ1 = ζ - π/2; β = π/2 - ψ1; ρ = ψ1 - φ_a. Legend: MT = Measured Log Thickness; VT = True Vertical Thickness; VE = True Stratigraphic Thickess; φ_a = Apparent Bed Dip along Directional Well Path; ψ1 = Angle of Well Drilled Up-dip.

figures.label: Figure 4-21 (c)
figures.description: TYPE 2 detailed wellbore/formation geometry used to derive the Type 2 correction factor. Formation Top and Formation Base dip to the right; the directionally drilled well runs steeply from upper-left through point T on the formation top down through V to point M on the formation base, with perpendicular construction to point C (right angles marked) and point S on the base. Angles labelled: ζ, φ_a, ζ - φ_a, ψ2, and γ at M. Accompanying relations: ψ2 = π/2 - ζ; γ = ψ2 + φ_a. Legend: MT = Measured Thickness; VT = True Vertical Thickness; ST = True Stratigraphic Thickess; φ_a = Apparent Bed Dip along Directional Well Path; ψ2 = Angle of Well Drilled Down-dip.
